text:
Alex Killorn is 37, has two Stanley Cups from Tampa, and is still playing 16 and a half minutes a night for an Anaheim team that has mostly been winning around him. His own numbers have stalled: six points in 20 games, two goals, and zero goals in his last ten.

This is a bad-luck stretch more than a decline, at least so far. The Ducks have scored 6.5 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and he's shooting 7.1% against a usual rate near 12. At five on five Anaheim is six points better in shot share with him than without. Our range has his point pace well above where it sits now.

What he brings hasn't changed much. He kills penalties, he plays the way Sean Couturier and Jordan Martinook play, and Evolving-Hockey had him at 0.7 wins above replacement last season, mostly from even-strength offense. He's past 1,000 career games and 572 points coming into the year. The question for the rest of the season is age: whether the chances stay this steady while the legs get older.
